Chapter 7: Breaking the Cycle of Rumination and Building Forward Momentum
Let’s talk about something that can quietly chip away at your confidence—even when you're not fully aware it’s happening. Rumination.
You know that feeling when your mind keeps replaying a mistake or a bit of tough feedback over and over? It’s like a mental loop that just won’t stop. Sure, reflecting on what happened can be useful, but when it turns into rumination, it usually just stirs up more self-doubt and anxiety.
This habit can show up even more in high-achieving professionals—especially those who set the bar really high for themselves. Maybe after a difficult meeting, or when you get a piece of criticism, you find yourself going over every detail, wondering what you could’ve done differently. Over time, this can drain your energy, making it way harder to take risks or move forward.
So, how do you break out of that cycle? Let’s look at some simple habits that can help you learn and keep moving forward:
First, when a mistake happens, try asking yourself, “What can I learn from this?” instead of, “Why did I do that?” See the difference? One invites growth, while the other just keeps you stuck.
Next, set a time limit for reflection. Give yourself permission to process what happened, but then make a conscious effort to shift your focus. It’s like saying, “Alright, I’ve thought this through—now it’s time to move forward.”
Grounding techniques really help, too. Maybe you take a few deep breaths, or step outside for a short walk after something stressful. These small actions can reset your mind and help you break out of that mental spin.
And remember, you don’t have to handle this alone. Talk things over with a trusted colleague or mentor. Sometimes, just hearing someone else’s perspective can help you reality-check your thoughts and see things more clearly.
Think of rumination like being stuck in a revolving door. The goal is to step out of that loop and onto the path ahead. By focusing on learning and action instead of harsh self-criticism, you’ll find it a lot easier to build resilience—and keep your momentum going.
